title: NRC opens comments on draft EA for Crownpoint ISR project
summary: Through December 21, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission is accepting public comments on a draft environmental assessment (EA), a draft programmatic agreement (PA), and a finding of no significant impact (FONSI) for an in situ recovery (ISR) uranium mining project covering four locations in McKinley County, N.M. NuFuels, a subsidiary of Laramide Resources, has applied for a renewal of license SUA-1580 to construct and operate the Crownpoint Uranium Project (CUP), also known as the Crownpoint–Church Rock Uranium Project. Permitting processes for the project are being expedited under the federal FAST-41 program, with final reviews expected to be completed in May 2027. If approved, the renewed license would cover construction and operation of the project for 20 years.

title: IEA’s World Energy Outlook 2026 looks at nuclear power’s future amid global turmoil
summary: The global crises currently impacting energy supply and demand have countries looking inward to solve their energy needs. A shift toward more domestic energy resources ultimately should help nuclear energy, the International Energy Agency argued in its latest annual World Energy Outlook. The energy market impacts of the conflicts in the Middle East and the resulting disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz echo the oil crises of the 1970s. According to the World Energy Outlook 2026, issued on November 19, the current global moment should reinforce the resurgence of nuclear power.

title: INL Computing Facility becomes DOE-NE user facility, launches Arco
summary: The Department of Energy’s Office of Nuclear Energy has designated the Idaho National Laboratory Computing Facility (INLCF) as an official user facility, making it the first such facility in the United States for high-performance computing focused on nuclear energy research. Christian Natoni, the deputy manager for facilities, programs, and partnerships at the DOE Idaho Operations Office, said, “Making these computing resources available as a DOE Office of Nuclear Energy user facility gives researchers across the nuclear energy community access to capabilities they need to tackle complex challenges.”

title: Pacific Fusion Gets Key Licence For $1 Billion New Mexico Demonstration Facility
summary: US-based Pacific Fusion announced that the New Mexico Environment Department (NMED) has approved its radioactive materials licence, enabling the company to operate a fusion machine and accelerate its efforts to bring fusion energy to the grid. The licence authorises Pacific Fusion to possess and use tritium for fusion at its $1bn (€910m) research and manufacturing campus in Albuquerque, a facility that will house its demonstration fusion system. The company said this is the first radioactive materials licence New Mexico has ever issued to a private fusion company, and enables key research supporting the company’s goal of net facility gain by 2030, generating more energy output than the energy used to power the system.
